subject: Re: Redwood Dedicated vs Hyperscaler options — next steps & capacity Qs
messages:
From: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.inference>

Cc: rishi_malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.inference>, priyom_das <priyom.das@redwood.inference>
Date: Thu, 8 Jul 2026 13:30:00 -0700
Subject: Redwood Dedicated vs Hyperscaler options — follow-up and next steps

Hi Samir —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned: 

- Recap: AtlasHealth is evaluating two tracks: hyperscaler-hosted GPU endpoints (reserved VMs/GPU pools) vs Redwood Dedicated (reserved GPU pools with SLA and burst). Your primary requirements are predictable latency at 95th percentile < 120ms for inference, guaranteed capacity during scheduled batch windows, and SOC2-level auditability.
- Differentiators we discussed from Redwood side:
  - Dedicated capacity with reservation guarantees, autoscale policies and burst buffers to cover scheduled runs
  - Prefix/KV caching and continuous batching to lower per-token costs while meeting latency SLOs
  - Observability and per-route cost/latency breakdowns for chargeback and SRE metrics

Proposed next steps: 
1) I will share a short matrix comparing Redwood Dedicated vs a representative hyperscaler reserved-GPU setup (attached).
2) Can you share the target monthly committed GPU hours and the peak concurrent requests you expect during your nightly consolidation window? Those numbers will let us size a Dedicated proposal and run a cost/latency estimate.
3) If procurement needs it, we can provide a short POC scope (2-week POC) to validate latency and capacity guarantees.

Please reply with the capacity numbers and any procurement constraints (PO process/timing). If it helps, we can also set up a technical deep-dive with our infra lead (Rishi) early next week.

Thanks,
Laura
Laura Bennett
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Laura —

Appreciate the clear recap. Couple of clarifications from our side: 

- For the nightly consolidation window we are targeting 1,200 concurrent requests (batched inference jobs) for a 2 hour window. Month-to-month average is ~400 GPU hours but we have spikes tied to quarterly runs — approximately 6x baseline.
- Procurement: standard PO + SOC2 evidence required; target to finalize vendor by end of August.
- Key ask re hyperscalers: they’ve offered reserved GPU instances with a 12‑month commitment and aggressive list-price discounts. We need to understand the true operational difference — is the value primarily in observability/rollout tooling and guaranteed capacity, or are there execution-level kernel/latency advantages with Redwood?

Also looping in procurement (procurement@atlashealth.com) for heads up on timelines.

—Samir

Laura / team / Samir —

Short answers and proposed wording for the customer: 

- Capacity guarantees: Yes — Redwood Dedicated supports reserved GPU pools with a contract-backed SLA for capacity during scheduled windows. We can provision a pool sized to handle 1,200 concurrent batched requests for the 2-hour window and configure burst capacity. The burst buffer is implemented as reserve nodes plus pre-warmed kernels and KV cache warmup to absorb transient spikes.
- Latency: With model-specific kernel selection, quantization to int4/int8 where acceptable, and continuous batching tuned for AtlasHealth’s request distribution, 95p < 120ms is achievable in our testing. We’ll validate during POC with their production-ish traces.
- Hyperscaler vs Redwood operational difference: Hyperscalers give VM-level reservations but don’t provide model-aware batching/kv-cache optimizations out of the box or the same per-route observability. That’s where we differentiate: lower effective per-token cost with similar or better latency at scale, plus rollout/rollback and deterministic fallbacks.

Priyom — if you can send a 2-line delta cost estimate, I’ll inline it into the summary for Samir. Otherwise I can craft a short technical note for procurement (SOC2 evidence + POC validation plan).

—Rishi
Senior Infra Lead, Redwood Inference
